fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly, as the single entry and exit point means responders need to identify it quickly on arrival.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so fire apparatus and ambulances can reach both structures without delay.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area within the property so emergency vehicles are not required to back out onto the road.
• Cut back dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure to allow responders to move between buildings on foot.
• Mark or establish a walking path from the front of the property to the rear so responders arriving on foot can move quickly to limited rear-access areas.
• Keep the patio area free of stored items so it can be used as a staging area if needed during an emergency.
• Confirm the parking area can accommodate at least one emergency vehicle without blocking the access drive.
• Post the address visibly on both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can identify each building separately.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim all shrubs and low tree branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls and roof edges.
• Thin the scattered trees and shrubs surrounding the house to create open gaps between individual plants and the structure.
• Remove woody debris such as fallen branches, logs, and dead plant material from around the house and any outbuildings.
• Clear brush growing along both sides of the driveway to maintain an open travel path for vehicles.
• Trim overhanging tree branches above the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Separate shrub clusters near the house by removing plants between groupings so vegetation is not continuous from the surrounding area to the structure.
• Remove or thin brush in the area immediately behind the house where rear access is limited.
• Keep the area directly around the house clear of loose woody material, dry plant debris, and piled brush.
• Thin scattered shrubs on the open terrain surrounding the house to reduce how closely vegetation connects to the structure.
• Remove dead branches and woody debris from beneath trees near the house.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible and easy to locate from the main road.
• Keep the single access route free of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris that could block entry or exit.
